subject: [DevOps] Logging and monitoring basics
description: Logging and monitoring basics. In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform, in the `cell` module) and **ticvai-backend**: the OpenTelemetry SDK (already referenced by the starter) in each of the five deployables of ADR-0055 (commerce, access, operations, workers and ticvai-ai), exporting traces, metrics and logs over OTLP to an OpenTelemetry Collector in the cell, which writes them to the cell's Log Analytics workspace in Azure UAE North (audit R057; nothing leaves the region). Logs are structured, never concatenated, and carry the trace and correlation ids; they never hold guest names, emails, phone numbers, document numbers, card data or biometric templates, only the opaque subject id (docs/architecture/observability.md; ADR-0009: PII-free by construction, not by filtering). Metrics are Prometheus-compatible. One alert rule to start with (the 5xx rate of each host) goes to an Azure Monitor action group that emails the on-call person (DevOps until a rota exists). Dev and staging only; production is built before the first live tenant. Done when: a request to a dev host can be followed from its log line to its trace by the correlation id; a deliberate 500 on a dev host raises an alert the on-call person receives within five minutes; and a search of a day's dev logs after the seeded test run finds no email address, phone number or card number.

Four .NET hosts in one solution: commerce (Identity, Tenancy, Catalogue, Order, Ledger, Wallet), access (Access), operations (F&B, Retail, Inventory, VenueOps, Marketing, WhiteLabel, Reporting, Platform, CrossRegion) and workers (the outbox relay, every module's event consumers, scheduled jobs), each composing its modules through IModule. ticvai-ai stays the Python service. subject: [BE] Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring
description: Qdrant cluster in dev and staging: 3 nodes, TLS, snapshots, monitoring. Builds: `adr ADR-0049`, `adr ADR-0021`. In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform): a self-hosted 3-node Qdrant cluster in Azure UAE North for dev and staging (ADR-0049), pinned to 1.16 or later, with TLS, JWT RBAC on and the signing key in the cell's Key Vault, snapshot storage in the UAE, and monitoring and alerts on node health, disk and latency. Check Qdrant Hybrid Cloud on our own AKS as an alternative before building. Done when: the cluster survives the loss of one node, a snapshot of a test collection restores into a fresh cluster, and a request without a valid token is refused.

subject: [BE] Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage
description: Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage. Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0016`. A deriver reads handoff/api-data-lineage.json and generates, per owning module, the views other modules may read (894 cross-schema reads on 30 September; ADR-0055), applied by the migrations. Done when: every cross-schema read in the Block A slice goes through a published view, the views regenerate with one command, and a raw cross-schema read is reported by the lineage check. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), ADR-0055 rule 2: another module reads a schema only through views its owner publishes (or the owner's in-process query interface), never raw tables; the owner is the schema's module in handoff/service-decomposition.json. Default for the shape: one view per (reader module, owned table) pair the lineage actually reads, in the owner's schema, named `<table>_for_<reader module>`, exposing only the columns the reader's operations read, with SELECT granted to the reader's deployable role (DB-ROLES). Reads routed `analytical` go to the reporting replica, never the primary (ADR-0016).

subject: [BE] One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only
description: One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only. Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0020`. In ticvai-backend, created by the baseline migration (MIG-BASELINE), one PostgreSQL login role per deployable of ADR-0055: commerce, access, operations, workers and ticvai_ai, each reading its password or token from the cell's Key Vault. Each role gets USAGE and SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on the schemas its modules own (the schema owners in handoff/service-decomposition.json; workers runs every module's consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs, so it gets the schemas those touch), SELECT on the published read views of DB-READ-VIEWS, and nothing else: no CREATE, no ownership, no BYPASSRLS, so FORCE row-level security applies to every host. ticvai_ai writes only the ai schema (and ai.inbox; ADR-0058) and is read-only on the transactional schemas (ADR-0020). The tables are owned by a separate migration role that only SqlMigrationRunner uses. Done when: each host connects with its own role from Key Vault; an INSERT from the ticvai_ai role into a transactional table, and from the commerce role into an operations schema (fnb), are each refused by PostgreSQL; no host role has BYPASSRLS or owns a table (a query on pg_roles and pg_tables in CI shows it); and a host role with no scope set on its session reads no rows from a table under FORCE row-level security. The schemas each role owns (handoff/service-decomposition.json under ADR-0055's five deployables, 4 October, CHG-FXP-005): commerce: identity, pii, platform, workforce, approvals, accreditation, tenancy, kernel, catalogue, pricing, promotions, seating, orders, payments, ledger, wallet; access: access; operations: inventory, fnb, retail, marketing, queue, maintenance, resources, venuemap, assets, games, rental, transport, subscription, whitelabel, reporting, sync (and control, in the control database, ADR-0039); ticvai_ai: ai (and ai.inbox), read-only on the rest; workers: the schemas its consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs write, which is every module's.

subject: [BE] Migration fan-out across tenant databases, and expand-then-contract changes
description: Migration fan-out across tenant databases, and expand-then-contract changes. Builds: `table control.migration`, `table control.migration_run`, `table control.migration_run_cell`, `table control.migration_run_tenant`, `table control.migration_plan_cell`, `adr ADR-0039`. Apply a migration to every tenant database with progress and resume, and the rule that a schema change ships in two steps so old and new code both run (SD-049). Done when: a column rename reaches three seeded tenant databases with no downtime. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), ADR-0039 section 3: the fan-out unit is a tenant database and the canary is a tenant inside a canary cell; one `control.migration_run_tenant` row per tenant per run (status, from_version, to_version, error, timings), with `control.migration_run_cell` as the rollup; `control.migration_plan_cell` names all tenants of a cell or a named set. subject: [BE] Observability with tenant and venue on every trace, and the first dashboards
description: Observability with tenant and venue on every trace, and the first dashboards. Builds: `operation orders#createOrder`, `operation orders#createPayment`, `operation orders#syncOrders`, `operation access#syncScans`, `operation access#validateAccess`. OpenTelemetry attributes for tenant, venue and workstation; dashboards for the sale path and sync; alerts on error rate and latency (SD-048). Done when: a failed POS sale can be found by venue and till within a minute. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), docs/architecture/observability.md: every log, metric and span carries tenant_id, region_id and venue_id (plus cell, correlation and session id on traces, and workstation on POS metrics), set by the kernel from the resolved session and the workstation. The sale path is the operations linked here (createOrder and createPayment in OrderService, validateAccess in AccessService); sync is syncOrders and syncScans. The first alerts are that document's list (outbox backlog per device, replication lag per cell, PgBouncer pool saturation, Redis-Postgres capacity divergence, the venue edge heartbeat) on the stack SETUP-OBS sets up.

subject: [BE] Request kernel: hostname to tenant routing, per-transaction scope, error model and 429
description: Request kernel: hostname to tenant routing, per-transaction scope, error model and 429. Builds: `table control.tenant_domain`, `table control.tenant`, `table control.cell_tenant`, `table platform.scope`, `adr ADR-0038`, `adr ADR-0039`, `adr ADR-0005`. In ticvai-backend. Resolve the tenant from the hostname (control-plane routing table, SD-021), open every transaction with the tenant and scope settings the row-level policies read (SD-059), one problem-details error model, and 429 with Retry-After on the hot public operations (SD-043). Done when: two seeded tenants on two hostnames cannot read each other's rows, and a flood test returns 429 instead of 500. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the routing table is `control.tenant_domain` (hostname, verified, redirect) in the control database, joined to `control.tenant` and `control.cell_tenant` for the tenant's cell and database (ADR-0038: one database per tenant inside its region's cell; ADR-0039: `control` is a database of its own and `control.cell` has no tenant_id, the relation is `control.cell_tenant`). The row-level policies of backend/tenant/920-row-level-security.sql read two session settings, set with SET LOCAL at the start of every transaction from the resolved session: `ticvai.scope_paths` (the comma-separated ltree scope paths the principal may see; unset or empty means no rows) and `ticvai.subject_id` (the guest's own rows). Venues stay partitions of the tenant database (ADR-0005), not databases.

subject: [BE] Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica
description: Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica. Builds: `operation subscription#getPlan`, `adr ADR-0032`, `adr ADR-0064`. ADR-0064 (accepted 1 October), in the kernel middleware of the commerce, access and operations hosts: a token bucket per tenant and audience (guest/public, staff, service, partner) with counts shared through Azure Managed Redis, sustained rate and a 2x burst for 10 seconds from the tenant's plan (Plan.requestLimits) or the platform default; one tenant held to 25% of a replica's request slots only while the replica is above 70% of its limit; shedding guest and public first, staff and service last (ADR-0032); 429 with Retry-After and the RateLimit-* headers; if Redis is unavailable each replica falls back to its own in-process buckets (the limit divided by the replica count). Done when: in a test with two tenants on one replica, the busy tenant gets the whole replica while the other is quiet, is held to 25% of the slots once the replica passes 70% while the quiet tenant's requests still succeed, a guest burst never spends a till's staff budget, and stopping Redis leaves requests served under the in-process limits. Contract (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the plan's limits are `Plan.requestLimits` in contracts/satellite/subscription.yaml (read with `subscription#getPlan`); the refusal is the shared `rate-limited` problem (429) of contracts/shared/common.yaml with `Retry-After` and the RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers it defines.

subject: [BE] Release flags per tenant
description: Release flags per tenant. Half-built features stay dark per tenant between sprints (SD-051). Spec (default taken 4 October, CHG-FXP-005; for the lead to confirm): flags live in Azure App Configuration in the cell's region, read by every .NET host through Microsoft.FeatureManagement with a tenant targeting filter; a flag's key is an app-module key of the plan (for example `AM-MARKETING-CRM-P01`) and covers that app-module's screens and the operations they bind (their `apis` in screens/*.yaml). Off for a tenant: the apps leave its screens out of that tenant's navigation, and the kernel answers its operations with the shared 404 problem of contracts/shared/common.yaml, as if absent. Done when: with one app-module's flag off for tenant A only, A's guest web no longer shows that module's screens and its operations return 404 for A, while tenant B still sees and calls them; switching it back on restores A within a minute.

subject: [BE] Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ
description: Outbox, relay and inbox behind the kernel broker interface, on a local RabbitMQ. Builds: `table platform.outbox`, `table kernel.inbox`, `table platform.dead_letter`, `table control.outbox_relay`, `adr ADR-0033`, `adr ADR-0057`, `adr ADR-0058`. The transactional outbox per tenant database; one relay per region in the workers host, with a lease and a polling loop per tenant database, and an inbox per tenant database for exactly-once handling (ADR-0058); modules enqueue through IOutbox inside their own transaction, the relay publishes through IBrokerPublisher and consumers subscribe through IEventSubscriber (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October); the relay drains a full batch at once and its batch size is configuration (Relay:BatchSize, 1,000 in the flash-sale environment). The broker per ADR-0057 is the client's choice between RabbitMQ and Kafka: build behind the kernel interface on a local RabbitMQ until they answer, with ordering per aggregate by an ordering key and dead letters drained into platform.dead_letter. A relay-lag dashboard and alert per tenant database (SD-030, SD-031, SD-032). Done when: an event written in a transaction reaches its consumer once, survives a relay restart and a redelivery, a poison message lands in platform.dead_letter, and relay lag shows on the dashboard and alerts when unpublished rows are older than 60 seconds.

subject: [BE] Row-level policies without a per-row subquery on hot tables
description: Row-level policies without a per-row subquery on hot tables. Builds: `table orders.sales_order`, `table access.scan_event`, `table platform.scope`, `adr ADR-0005`, `adr ADR-0044`. Scope predicates read session settings instead of joining per row (SD-016). Done when: the order and scan-event queries keep their plan with policies on, measured on the seed data. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): the policies are generated in backend/tenant/920-row-level-security.sql by `platform.apply_scope_rls` and its siblings; today each USING clause calls `platform.in_scope(scope_path)`, which unnests `ticvai.scope_paths` for every row. On the hot tables (the order and scan-event tables linked here, partitioned by venue_id with venue_id leading the key: ADR-0044, ADR-0005), rewrite the predicate so the planner evaluates the session setting once per statement (an InitPlan over `platform.current_scope_paths()`, or a `venue_id = ANY(...)` predicate that keeps partition pruning) instead of per row; the policy names and deny-by-default stay. Measured with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on the seed data before and after.

subject: [BE] Payment adapter and signed webhook against the provider's test mode
description: Payment adapter and signed webhook against the provider's test mode. Builds: `operation payments#receivePaymentProviderWebhook`, `table payments.provider_event`. The provider adapter, the inbound signed webhook, the provider reference on payments, 3-D Secure redirect states and the card-terminal flow for the POS (SD-034). Done when: an approved, a declined and a 3-D Secure payment each end in the right order state from the webhook alone, with polling only as the fallback. Acceptance of the declined, unknown and reconcile paths waits on the client's payment sandbox credentials: see the client's answer in the Decisions Register. Until the client's sandbox credentials arrive (CLIENT-PAY-SANDBOX), the three outcomes are proven with signed webhook fixtures built from the provider's documented test payloads and a locally generated signing secret (CHG-FXP-006); the run against the provider's test mode follows when they arrive and is the acceptance of those paths.

subject: [BE] Republish from the outbox by tenant and time range
description: Republish from the outbox by tenant and time range. Builds: `operation platform-ops#republishOutbox`, `operation platform-ops#getOutboxRepublish`, `operation platform-ops#listOutboxRepublishes`, `operation platform-ops#cancelOutboxRepublish`, `table control.outbox_republish`, `adr ADR-0058`. The recovery path for a lost broker (ADR-0058 amendment, 1 October; the DR design in ADR-0060 relies on it): republishOutbox, listOutboxRepublishes, getOutboxRepublish and cancelOutboxRepublish in the operations host, carried out by the relay in workers with a keyset cursor over the outbox, published_at left untouched and live batches first; one job per tenant (control.outbox_republish). Done when: after a simulated broker loss, a republish of one tenant's last hour redelivers every event once to each consumer, the inbox drops the duplicates, and a second request for the same tenant while one runs is refused with 409.

subject: [BE] Order paid to tickets issued: the saga proven end to end
description: Order paid to tickets issued: the saga proven end to end. Builds: `operation orders#createPayment`, `operation catalogue#convertInventoryHold`, `operation access#issueOrderEntitlements`, `table access.entitlement`, `table catalogue.inventory_hold`, `table catalogue.channel_capacity`, `table ledger.journal_entry`, `table ledger.journal_line`, `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0058`. order.paid consumed by the entitlement owner, tickets issued, the ledger posting once from the event, and holds converted with capacity decremented (SD-026, SD-023). Done when: a web purchase in the sandbox ends with a ticket, one ledger posting and sold capacity reduced, and a replayed event changes nothing. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), from events/order-paid.yaml and events/entitlement-issued.yaml (adam_search order.paid): the payment transaction (createPayment, or the provider webhook) converts the inventory holds (`catalogue#convertInventoryHold`: the hold becomes sold capacity), posts the cash receipt to ledger.journal_entry and ledger.journal_line, and writes `order.paid` to the outbox in the same transaction; AccessService consumes it (`access#issueOrderEntitlements`, idempotency key orderId + lineId; on failure retry, then dead-letter, which pages) and publishes `entitlement.issued`; the orders consumer of that completes the order. A dead-lettered issuance is replayed, never compensated by an automatic refund. ADR-0055: modules in different deployables talk by event; ADR-0058: one relay per region and an inbox per tenant database, so a replayed event is a no-op.

subject: [BE] Alerts on one tenant's share of its connection pool and on max_connections
description: Alerts on one tenant's share of its connection pool and on max_connections. Builds: `adr ADR-0032`, `adr ADR-0064`. ADR-0064 item 4: per-tenant pool caps stay, and two alerts watch them: one tenant holding more than 60% of its pool for five minutes, and the instance passing 80% of max_connections; plus a dashboard panel of 429s per tenant and audience from KERNEL-TENANT-LIMITS. Done when: a load run that holds one tenant's pool fires the first alert after five minutes naming the tenant, and opening connections past 80% of max_connections fires the second. Where the numbers come from (4 October, CHG-FXP-005): one tenant's share is PgBouncer's SHOW POOLS for that tenant database (cl_active plus cl_waiting against pool_size); the instance figure is the count of pg_stat_activity against max_connections; both are scraped into the Prometheus-compatible metrics of SETUP-OBS and alert through its Azure Monitor action group, labelled with tenant_id and cell.

subject: [AI] AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering
description: AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering. Builds: `operation ai#setAiCredential`, `operation ai#setAiProvider`, `operation ai#evaluateAiGovernance`, `operation ai#getAiUsage`, `operation ai#testAiProvider`, `table ai.activity`, `table ai.decision_record`, `table ai.provider`, `adr ADR-0009`, `adr ADR-0020`. setAiCredential, setAiProvider are served by ticvai-ai behind the AI gateway, to their contracts at the release tag in ADAM; no back-end task builds them. In ticvai-ai (Python). One gateway every AI call goes through: capability code calls gateway.run(task, inputs, schema?) and never names a provider (design 3.3). **Routing, in order:** (1) the allowed set: TICVAI's curated catalogue, filtered by the tenant's AI residency class (ADR-0009 amended 2 October, DEC-539): uaeOnly, the default and mandatory for government, bank and health tenants, resolves only to endpoints inside the UAE (Core42 Compass GPT-4.1 mini for the Small tier, Compass GPT-5 for the Strong tier, reached through the existing openaiCompatible provider kind); globalAllowed (a private venue under PDPL Art. 23) resolves to Azure gpt-5-mini / gpt-6-sol Global Standard or the tenant's BYOK provider; onPrem only when a client asks for it, and nothing is built for it in Block A (we host no model: Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-004); then by the task's data classification and the governance policy; (2) the task's tier from TICVAI's curated task-to-tier map: a client never picks a model. BYOK accepts any vendor (CHG-FUP-008), is enabled by TICVAI (PLATFORM_AI_MANAGE) for a globalAllowed tenant only, maps each task to that vendor's equivalent model, and is activated by setAiProvider only after testAiProvider's compatibility probes pass (tool calling, structured output, Arabic, context, latency, residency); the key is a per-tenant write-only Key Vault secret shown only by its last four characters; (3) the cascade, Small to Strong only on a checkable signal (schema validation failed twice, retrieval partial), never on a model's self-reported confidence; (4) a circuit breaker per endpoint (opens at 50% errors over 20 calls or p95 above twice the task budget for 60 s; half-open after 30 s) and the class's fallback chain (uaeOnly: Core42 Compass, then OpenAI's UAE region; no model is hosted in the cell, so with both down the call goes to degraded mode); a residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region; (5) degraded mode when nothing answers (search-only, rules-only or 'a person will help'). **Before each call:** the per-request budget and the capability's ceilingBehaviour, maskedFields (fail closed), then the scrubber and input guard of AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD, and a stable-first prompt order for prefix caching. **After it:** structured-output validation, the output guard and the re-fill, an ai.activity row and OpenTelemetry spans with no prompt text. evaluateAiGovernance is an in-process decision point (allow, allow with conditions, prepare only, approval required, escalate, block, with the policy version; design 3.8); getAiUsage meters tokens and spend per tenant; every governed answer writes one ai.decision_record (model, prompt template, policy and knowledge versions; design 3.9). About 12 engineer-days. **setAiProvider and setAiCredential are served here** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-001): in Block A TICVAI staff enter a tenant's BYOK provider and key under the platform-staff grant on ADM-037 (no tenant self-service yet); the provider is checked against the curated catalogue and the tenant's residency class, and the key goes to the cell's Key Vault, never to a table in clear. About one engineer-day more (13). **Failover, in full** (DEC-539 as amended 3 October; CHG-R1S-001, CHG-R1S-002): a uaeOnly call goes to Core42 Compass by default and falls back only to OpenAI's UAE region (the ae.api.openai.com project); no model is hosted in the cell (we host none unless a client asks: Chinmay, 3 October), so with both down it answers in degraded mode. A residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region, and failover never widens residency (CHG-R1S-016); global endpoints are called statelessly (no Assistants, Threads or Conversations, store=false, no uploads or fine-tuning). Done when: a uaeOnly tenant's call reaches the Compass endpoint and, with Compass forced down, falls back to the OpenAI UAE endpoint, and with both forced down answers in degraded mode, never from a Global endpoint (a test asserts the residency refusal instead of a cross-border call); a BYOK provider that fails a compatibility probe is refused with 409 compatibility-test-required; a tenant over its ceiling gets the capability's ceilingBehaviour; and every call in the test run leaves an ai.activity row, and every governed answer a decision record naming its model, prompt and policy versions.

subject: [AI] Help me choose: suggested question sets from the product catalogue
description: Help me choose: suggested question sets from the product catalogue. Builds: `operation white-label#proposeGuidedChoice`, `operation white-label#publishGuidedChoice`, `table ai.guided_choice_suggestion`. In ticvai-ai: Help me choose suggested from the catalogue (design 3.11, decided 29 September; capability C7 at autonomy 'suggest'). Rules first: read each guest-sellable product's category, subcategory, segment tags (level, audience), minimum height and age, duration, price band and language through the catalogue API with the venue's permissions; pick the one or two attributes that split the products most evenly, dropping any where one answer leaves nothing bookable (deterministic: the same catalogue gives the same questions); map each answer to a product, a category or a flow. The Small tier writes the question, answer titles and one-liners in the tenant's languages from the attributes only, never guest data; with the model unavailable the attribute names are used as they are. The draft is saved through proposeGuidedChoice (source aiSuggested, suggestionRef) with a decision record of the inputs, the split each question makes and the model and prompt versions. Publishing is publishGuidedChoice by a person holding TENANT_PUBLISH; nothing is published automatically. A withdrawn mapped product, or new products no answer reaches, raise a new suggestion and never rewrite the published version. About 4 engineer-days. Done when: the same catalogue run twice gives the same questions; the draft lands with source aiSuggested and a decision record; with the model stubbed down a usable draft still lands with attribute names; nothing is live until a person publishes; and withdrawing a mapped product raises a new suggestion.

subject: [AI] Qdrant tenancy: a collection and a scoped token per tenant, the retrieval client, erasure and snapshots
description: Qdrant tenancy: a collection and a scoped token per tenant, the retrieval client, erasure and snapshots. Builds: `table ai.chunk_embedding`, `adr ADR-0049`, `adr ADR-0021`. Collection-per-tenant provisioning at tenant onboarding, per embedding model (t_<tenantId>_<model>) behind the alias tenant_<tenantId> (a model change is a shadow collection, an evaluation and an alias swap); per-tenant HS256 JWT issuance and rotation, scoped to the tenant's collections and alias, signed with the admin API key that only the issuer reads from Key Vault (ticvai-ai never does); the single retrieval client with no scope parameter that reads the caller's scope from the request and always adds the venue filter (points carry venue_id and scope_path, indexed); dense and sparse named vectors fused by reciprocal rank; erasure by guest or document payload, checked against the point references in ai.chunk_embedding; offboarding that deletes the collections and alias and revokes the token; per-collection snapshots copied to UAE North storage by a CronJob (azcopy, workload identity) and a restore tested per tenant. subject: [AI] Venue-map proposals: walkways from a raster plan and labels for extracted shapes
description: Venue-map proposals: walkways from a raster plan and labels for extracted shapes. Builds: `table ai.proposed_action`, `adr ADR-0069`. In ticvai-ai: the AI side of proposeWalkways and proposeVenueLabels for the venue-map import that ships in r1 (CHG-RONEC-001; BO-093 Map Import & Labelling, BO-094; ADR-0069; Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-AIPH-002). The operations' endpoints and their writes are the back-end tasks SVC-AI-AI-3 (proposeWalkways) and SVC-AI-AI-1 (proposeVenueLabels); this task is the model work behind them. Walkways: only for a raster plan (a scan, a photograph, an illustrated map, a scanned PDF read through the OCR step), where there is no geometry to subtract; where the import found hand-marked paths (VenueMapImportJob.handMarkedPaths) the proposal follows the marks, one segment per marked stretch between junctions with basis handMarked and a confidence for how cleanly the stroke was traced, a gap in a mark proposed as two segments and never bridged; otherwise basis auto or seen, with a confidence per segment, low-confidence segments shown and never filtered out. Labels: read the shapes venue-map.importVenueGeometry already extracted (never the drawing itself) and propose what each one is (kind and name), using scanned text near a shape as a hint (ocrHint says which text was used); text alone never creates a point or raises a proposal above what the shape supports. Both write ai.proposed_action through the gateway's decision point and stop: nothing is a path or a label until an operator accepts it, segment by segment (venue-map.acceptWalkwayProposals) and proposal by proposal (acceptVenueLabelProposals), on BO-093. The proposals are scrubbed and guarded like every call (AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD) and read only the tenant's own map and knowledge collection (ADR-0020; the label proposals read the venue's Qdrant collection, AI-ENGINE-QDRANT). An evaluation set of TICVAI's own drawings (raster plans with and without hand marks, CAD exports with labelled and unlabelled layers, Arabic and English text) joins the harness (AI-ENGINE-EVAL). With the provider down the import still completes: no proposals are raised and BO-093 says the AI proposals are unavailable, never an empty network presented as complete. About 2.5 engineer-days. Done when: a raster plan with hand-marked paths gets one proposed segment per marked stretch with basis handMarked and its confidence, and a gap stays a gap; a raster plan without marks gets segments with a confidence each, the low ones shown; extracted shapes get kind and name proposals that cite their ocrHint where they used scanned text; nothing is applied until an operator accepts it, segment by segment and proposal by proposal, on BO-093; it answers through the AI gateway with the scrubber and the guard on, its evaluation set passes the gate of docs/architecture/ai-system-design.md 3.5, it degrades as 3.7 says when its provider is down, and a peer AI engineer has reviewed it.

subject: [AI] The baseline-then-learn layer: estimator interface, maturity stages, venue profile, starting patterns
description: The baseline-then-learn layer: estimator interface, maturity stages, venue profile, starting patterns. Builds: `operation ai#setAiVenueSettings`, `table ai.capability_maturity`, `adr ADR-0051`. In ticvai-ai: the baseline-then-learn layer of design 3.13 (ADR-0051, AI-D16/AI-D17). **One estimator interface per question** (a suggestion kind, a forecast definition, a risk score, a recommendation rank) with three producers behind the same contract: the Prior (the venue AI profile from setAiVenueSettings, a starting pattern per venue type - water park, theme park, family entertainment centre, museum, arena, zoo or aquarium - written by TICVAI from published sources and never from another tenant's data, and the UAE calendar: Sat-Sun weekend, public holidays, Ramadan and Eid by Hijri date, school holidays, summer heat for outdoor venues); the Statistical producer, the tenant's own data pulled toward the prior, (k x prior + n x own mean) / (k + n) with k = coldStart.priorWeightObservations (4 same weekdays by default), re-estimated nightly as a recorded producer version; and the Learned slot, which only an admin's promotion fills (Block B). **Maturity on every answer:** AiMaturity (starting, learning, established, learned) on every Suggestion and AiForecastVersion and one ai.capability_maturity row per question, with the 'Based on' line (your venue profile, UAE calendar, 23 days of your sales), the share of own data and what the next stage needs. A 422 only for a missing setting (AiMissingSettingProblem names the setting and the screen that sets it), never for little history. The weather enters the prior with its Block B adapter. About 15 engineer-days; historical import, the training job and the learned producers continue in Block B. Done when: a new venue with no history gets an answer for every Block A suggestion kind on day one, with stage starting and a Based-on line; after 28 days of seeded sales the stage reads learning and the answer has moved toward the venue's own mean by the formula; a missing setting returns 422 naming it; and a two-tenant test shows no producer reads the other tenant's rows.

subject: [AI] PII scrubber in our worker and the provider's safety service in front of every LLM call

description: The planner agent on top of the rules planner. Builds: `operation venue-map#updateVisitPlan`, `table venuemap.visit_plan`.
